name: Root Cause Analysis Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for root cause analysis, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for root cause analysis, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer the simplest root cause analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
2. State assumptions about root cause analysis explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
3. Keep root cause analysis outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen root cause analysis approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Measure before optimizing any root cause analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Prefer explicit, readable root cause analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. Document any non-obvious root cause analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of root cause analysis correctness.
- Do not silently drop root cause analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic root cause analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting root cause analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated root cause analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for root cause analysis, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
